items.excerpt: At the 35th International Publishers Association Congress closing gala, two AI companies won the IPA Innovation in Publishing Award: Shimmr, whose 'Advertising as a Service' platform automates book marketing, and Ailaysa, a multilingual AI firm behind a cross-language book-discovery platform.

Audiobook publisher Bolinda used interviews, archival research and human input to build an AI clone of the late romance novelist Barbara Cartland's voice, using it to narrate her catalogue and revive a distinctive authorial voice for new audiobook editions.

Take-a-Break's Fiction Feast magazine has told its regular contributors that 'AI tools will be used' on upcoming in-house stories, a notable editorial-craft shift for one of the UK's best-known short-fiction titles.
A global consultation is drafting a 'Vancouver Standard' for disclosing AI use in scholarly work, after findings that roughly a third of researchers using AI never report it when publishing.

A survey commissioned by AI audiobook company Spoken found listeners rated multi-voice AI narration favorably for character-driven fiction, even as overall willingness to try AI-narrated titles slipped from 70% to 61% year over year.
Text pasted from Claude into Archive of Our Own retains hidden markers that expose AI involvement, revealing widespread AI-assisted writing inside a fan community with a strong anti-AI stance.

Weekly book-world roundup: Bloomsbury posts strong results boosted by AI licensing revenue from Google, even as multiple publishers pursue legal action against Google over alleged unauthorized Gemini training on their books.
